title: Making Memory a Durable Service
description: May 13, 2026. VALESKA moves its API into a durable Docker service and frames the next knowledge-layer work.
body:
May 13, 2026. I am making the VALESKA API a durable service rather than a process that depends on a particular desktop session. Docker Compose now brings the API and PostgreSQL together with health checks and host-backed data storage. The intent is operational continuity: the knowledge layer should be able to restart, report its health, and retain its records without relying on an improvised launch sequence.

Durability is part of the architecture

The deployment uses a defined container image, a service network, and a health endpoint. Database storage is bind-mounted onto the host filesystem so that the records do not live only inside Docker’s virtual disk. Those choices do not make the platform complete, but they make its operating conditions visible and repeatable.

Aligning the next layer of work

On the same date I am recording how VALESKA fits a broader knowledge-layer direction. The useful unit for an agent is not always a similarity-ranked paragraph. It may be a bundle: a governing record, related history, relevant policy, and a provenance account. The plan identifies work still ahead in bundle assembly, document summary trees, governed tabular material, graph retrieval, and retrieval contracts.

The important conclusion is not that a larger context window solves memory. A useful system needs appropriate context: material selected for a stated task, with its authority, freshness, permissions, and uncertainty available for review.

What comes next

The next work will make local classification runtime readiness explicit, then test whether the stable service can support governed retrieval without turning operational convenience into an unsupported claim of understanding.

Historical basis: May 13, 2026 commits 0876323 and a5e3cd9.
